During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:

 $NBIS just pulled off a $3.5B senior secured credit facility with Citi. First off accessing this level of institutional liquidity  without needing any immediate asset level contracts locked up is to me a a massive win that separates $NBIS from it's peers who is currently dragging $NBIS down. Let's dive deep in to how exactly this credit facility work, why management chose this structure and what the end game looks like.

1/ How the 364 day "credit line" work:
This isn't an amortizing loan where $NBIS starts dumping principal cash right away. It functions as a flexible bridge credit line. They draw funds as needed to build data centers and procure GPUs. The entire $3.5B principal sits as a hard lump-sum deadline at the end of the 364 days.   

2/ The 90 day step up pricing structure
The baseline interest starts at Term SOFR + 2.75%. To prevent $NBIS from treating this short term bank facility as permanent capital, Citi built in a step up penalty. Every 90 days  the borrowing margin ticks up by 25 bps until it caps out at SOFR + 3.50%. Still $NBIS has the flexibility to prepay and exit the loan at any time with zero prepayment penalty.   

3/ Why would $NBIS takes on short term bridge debt all of a sudden right now?
 Right now speed of bringing compute online is everything. Demand is scaling so fast that the return on getting physical clusters online immediately far outpaces a temporary ~3.5% spread over SOFR. Rather than spending 6 to 12 months negotiating slow, complex project finance debt up front, $NBIS takes rapid bank liquidity to capture hardware immediately which now has absurdly low payback periods. 4/ The sequencing plan
Management explicitly calls this "sequencing" capital. First, they use the $3.5B Citi bridge line to acquire GPUs and bring up clusters. Second, they attach these active sites to their pipeline of long term hyperscaler contracts (backed by over $40B in deal interest with $35B of that non optional). Once the sites are operational and cash flowing, $NBIS swaps out this bridge facility for long term, even lower cost asset backed securities (ABS) before the 364 day clock expires.

GoogleによるNvidiaのVera Rubinサーバーの大規模買収は、TSMC、Quanta、その他の企業に利益をもたらす。

11月21日、Googleは、Google CloudにNVIDIA Vera Rubin AIサーバーを導入し、最大96万個のRubin GPUを搭載するとともに、NVIDIAのConnectX-9 SuperNICイーサネットプラットフォームをGoogle CloudのVirgoネットワークアーキテクチャおよび第4世代の先進的な液冷技術と統合すると発表した。本格的な導入は11月に開始される予定。

アナリストたちは、Google CloudによるVera Rubin AIサーバーの大規模導入が新たなビジネスチャンスの波を引き起こし、TSMC （2330）、Quanta、Wistronといった台湾の関連企業に恩恵をもたらすと楽観視している。

中でも、フォックスコンやクアンタといった大手受託製造企業は、グーグルのAIサーバーサプライチェーンにおいて、主にNVIDIAのVera Rubinサーバーの供給を担っている。グーグルのTPUサーバーに対する需要の高まりに伴い、フォックスコンはグーグルからの受注をさらに獲得し、より力強い事業成長を遂げることが期待される。

Google Cloudは、Vera Rubin NVL 72システムレベル仕様を採用し、最大96万個のRubin GPUまで拡張して導入される予定です。Google Cloudは、NVIDIA AIサーバーをベアメタル方式で導入する業界初の顧客となります。

Google Cloudは、NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICイーサネットプラットフォームを使用し、Google CloudのVirgoネットワークアーキテクチャを統合することで、AIコンピューティングの効率性を向上させています。

業界の専門家は、Google VirgoアーキテクチャはAIデータセンター向けに特別に設計されたネットワークインターフェースであり、光通信仕様を強化し、帯域幅を拡大し、データ遅延を低減し、高速データ伝送路を構築するものだと指摘している。

業界アナリストは、Vera RubinはTSMCのCoWoS-L先進パッケージングプロセスを用いて製造されていると考えている。Google Cloudの受注状況に基づくと、Google CloudはTSMCのRubin工場の今後1～2年間の生産能力をほぼ予約済みであり、これは非常に大規模な計画である。

海外メディアの報道によると、GoogleのCEOであるサンダー・ピチャイ氏はインタビューで、同社の情報集約・収集業務の一部をAIに委任したと述べた。以前は社内で何が起こっているかを把握するのに毎日1時間かかっていたが、今ではAIが情報収集を支援できるようになったという。

ピチャイ氏は、AIはGoogleのモデル開発の進捗状況やコンピューティングリソースの使用状況を監視するために使用できるほか、業務効率を向上させるためのデータや分析を提供するようAIに依頼することもできると述べた。

彼は、AIはクラウド上で24時間稼働し、継続的にタスクを完了できるため、自分の時間を新しいタスクに充てることができると述べた。これがAIの最大の利点だ。

Expert Takeaways: TSMC

1. CoWoS Capacity, Fab Breakdown, Spill‑Over Orders & Customer Allocation

Capacity Expansion: TSMC's internal CoWoS monthly capacity is targeted to reach 130k wafers by end-2026, with a long-term goal of 260k wafers/month by 2028 (excluding OSAT volumes).

Demand Growth: Market demand for CoWoS has increased by at least 26% compared to early-2026 levels.

Fab Breakdown: AP8 full capacity is 50k wafers (>40k expected by end-2026); AP7-P1 reached its 35k full-load target after ramping in August; AP7-P2 focuses primarily on SoIC; US AP1 will not ramp significantly by year-end; legacy AP1–AP6 fabs handle the remaining volume.

Expansion Bottlenecks: New packaging fab construction takes about three years from groundbreaking to bottleneck-limited full output, constrained mainly by hybrid bonding and 3–4 nm-grade CMP flatness requirements.

OSAT Spill-Over Strategy: Lower-margin orders are routed to external OSATs (ASE, SPIL, Amkor) under signed LTAs, reserving TSMC’s internal capacity for high-value customers.

Customer Allocation Split: Nvidia (60%), Broadcom (15%), AMD (10%), Marvell (6%), AWS in-house silicon (5%), MediaTek (2%), and others (3%).

2. SoIC Capacity Roadmap, Capital Intensity, Fab Bottlenecks & End‑Use Drivers

Capacity Roadmap: Targeted at 15k wafers/month by end-2026, 24–28k by end-2027, and up to 45k by end-2028 (~90% CAGR in 2027).

Capital Intensity & Bottlenecks: Capital intensity is $6.8–7.0 billion per 10k monthly wafers. Hybrid-bonding pick-and-place tools are the initial bottleneck, shifting dynamically to PVD and PECVD.

Manufacturing Limits: High CMP flatness and particle cleanliness requirements create a hardware ceiling below CoWoS scale. Capacity is concentrated at Chiayi AP7 through end-2027 (long-term potential 40–50k/month). US AP1 will take future volume but faces a long learning curve requiring Taiwan team transfer.

Key Demand Drivers: Nvidia (Rubin Ultra / Feynman), AMD (MI400 / Venice), Apple (M5 Pro / Max), and Broadcom ASICs slated for 2027.

3. Competitive Landscape (Intel / Samsung), Yields & Risk Mitigation

Intel EMIB-T Status: Yield estimates vary from ~90% (supply chain) to 38–40% (test-vehicle data). EMIB-T die cost is ~50% of CoWoS-L. Intel outsources all backend assembly to Amkor across Longtan, Portugal, and Arizona.

Samsung & Competitor Scale: Samsung I-Cube yield maturity lags peers, with meaningful competitive threats unlikely until post-2030 when hybrid bonding matures. Overall, TSMC’s advanced packaging volume is ~5× that of Intel.

Customer De-Risking: Google is validating EMIB-T as a backup due to TSMC tightness, costs, and US policy. Broadcom is evaluating EMIB-T and Samsung capacity, while building a joint substrate/FC-BGA facility in Singapore with Toppan.

4. CoPoS Technical Bottlenecks, Production Timeline & Silicon Utilization

Realistic Timeline: Mass CoPoS production in 2027–2028 is overly optimistic. AP7 has started qualification, aiming for limited NPI in 2027, low-volume production (LVM) for Nvidia Feynman in H2-2028, and true high-volume manufacturing (HVM) in 2029–2030. Glass-core TGV technology is deferred to post-2030.

Technical Challenges: Five core bottlenecks include substrate warpage, fine-pitch RDL lithography, coat-and-plate uniformity, ~70% copper-fill yield for TGV vias, and large-format panel-tool standardization.

Fab Footprint & Wafer Efficiency: US AP2 is provisionally planned for CoPoS. CoPoS requires greenfield fabs and won't cannibalize CoWoS. For large die sizes (e.g., 75×75 mm), CoPoS panel utilization reaches >84%, compared to just 48% on 12-inch circular wafers.

5. TSMC Co-Development Model & CPO Technology Outlook

Deep Joint Development: Advanced packaging is not off-the-shelf; TSMC collaborates closely with key customers on architecture, process flow, equipment limits, photomasks, and probe cards (e.g., scaling SpaceX probe sites from 4–6 up to 32up).

CPO Reality: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) is not inherently tied to glass and can be built on silicon stacks. Key factors for success are I/O alignment precision and yield parity with CoWoS. Glass-based CPO currently faces high warpage and fracture risks.

6. Capital Expenditure, HPC Exposure & OSAT Dynamics

CapEx Upside: TSMC total capex guidance was revised up from $52–56B to $60–64B, with ~10% allocated to backend packaging (CoWoS/SooS).

Revenue Exposure: High Performance Computing (HPC) accounted for 68% of TSMC's Q3 revenue.

OSAT Role: External OSAT capacity serves purely as supplementary volume and cannot replace TSMC’s core leadership in high-end advanced packaging.

7. New-Fab Constraints, Capacity Methodology & Portfolio Strategy

Capacity Definition: Advanced-packaging fab capacity is defined by dynamic bottleneck tool stations (lithography, develop, die-bond, hybrid-bond) rather than physical floor space, creating variable output profiles across fabs.

A9/A10 & Future Fabs: Insider visibility on A9/A10 schedules remains limited with no firm dates.

Strategy: TSMC routes low-margin work externally while shifting internal capital toward next-gen CoPoS. Hybrid bonding and CMP flatness will remain recurring bottlenecks as Nvidia Feynman and HBM4-E ramp.

8. Supply-Chain Frictions from Constrained CoWoS-S Capacity

CoWoS-S Shortages: Shifted focus toward CoWoS-L has left CoWoS-S expansion constrained, weighing on 2026 customer deliveries.

Impacted Programs: TPU v7 / v8t implementations relying on CoWoS-S continue to face supply headwinds.

Alternative Approaches: Broadcom’s Sunfish uses CoWoS-L and is positioned well for 2027. Broadcom v8t and Humu-fish evaluated EMIB-T as an alternative, but yields remain inadequate, keeping supply pressure high on CoWoS-S programs.

> Supply capacity is about 60–75 million wafers, while demand reaches 260–300 million, a supply gap of over 70%.

> Building InP fabs and qualifying them takes at least 2–3 years.

> S/D ratio off InP EPI wafer supply trending towards 75% by 2030. 

CoWoS/CoPoS:

> Fubon estimates CoPoS monthly capacity: only ~5K wafers by 1Q28, ~30K by 4Q28. CoWoS: ~90K wafers in 2Q26, ~220K in 4Q28

> Nomura estimates TSMC CoWoS capacity: 675K wafers in 2025, 1.275M in 2026, 2.73M in 2027

Silicon Wafers:

> Global silicon wafer supply-demand gap will widen from about 8% at end-2026 to 15% in 2027 and 24% in 2028

> 12-inch wafer prices are expected to rise about 15–25% in 2027
